And next time. Let's turn to Deuteronomy chapter 18 tonight. If you're not familiar with our format, we're going to be here for about another hour studying The Old Testament, just fair warning for some of you who think that's like shocking to study the Bible that long, especially the Old Testament. That's what we're going to be doing. So, if you don't think you can hang with us, we understand sort of, and we will pray, and as we pray, you could get up and move into the foyer so that if you had to leave during the service, nobody would see you, you wouldn't disturb anybody. And other than that, we ask people, as we often announce Sunday morning as well, all the services to remain seated for the entire service. Tonight we'll be covering Deuteronomy 18 and 19. Let's pray. Father, what a privilege it is to gather together and to have fellowship, to pray together, to sing together, each song reminding us of who you are, your promises, and your power, the presence of the Holy Spirit among your people. We submit ourselves, Lord, to you, and to your word, your revelation. We know that you have given it in different stages throughout history, but that it reflects your mind, your heart. 0030f8fdb4bf.opening: Jeremiah 13 is the book and the chapter we'd like you to turn tonight, Jeremiah chapter 13. I'm not a perfect pastor, but I found the description of one. It was sent to Anne Landers, and she published it in her column. This is how it goes, the perfect pastor. The results of a computerized survey indicate the perfect pastor preaches at least 15 minutes. I blew that one. He condemned sin but never embarrasses anyone.
